messages:
Aisha: Hi all 1st day here7 — quick question for the new hires: any shorthand for where to post different kinds of stuff? e.g., I ran a big test log that I want feedback on, should it go in #eng or #eng-builds? Also etiquette for introducing myself across timezones?

Ben (people-ops): Welcome! :wave: Short guide: production logs and CI noise -> #eng-builds, code/design discussions with context -> team channel (#eng for infra, #eng-runtime for runtime), hiring/process questions -> #people-ops, benefits/payroll -> #finance or DM @people-ops for sensitive info. If you need broader eyes, start in the team channel and thread your log.

Claire (eng): For big logs, put a short summary in the thread and attach a Gist or link to an S3 object. Example: "build failed on test-x, logs: https://gist.github...; TL;DR failed on downstream mock." That keeps the channel readable. Use triple backticks for small snippets.

Aisha: Gotcha. And intros? I'm in PST, a few folks on CET. Do I post in #general or #new-hires?

Sam (onboarding): Post a one-paragraph intro in #general (name, role, timezone, a fun fact). Then paste a longer intro in #new-hires if you want feedback or onboarding tips. Note timezone in intro so people know when to DM. We usually pin intros for the week.

Claire (eng): A couple of quick etiquette items we've adopted: 1) use reactions (:eyes:, :thumbsup:) instead of "got it" replies when appropriate; 2) avoid pasting long stack traces into channel—use a link; 3) when you @mention a team, use a short subject on the first message like "[Infra] slow RPCs on staging" so it's scannable.

Aisha: Nice. What about bots — I saw Deploy-Bot post about a rollout. Can I trigger it?

Deploy-Bot: Only members of the deploy-approvers group can run `/deploy start`. To request a deploy, run `/deploy request --branch=...` and tag the approver. For rollouts triggered by CI failures, we post in #release-war-room automatically.

Ben (people-ops): Also: set your Slack timezone in profile (Preferences -> Language & region) so scheduled messages show correct times. Add pronouns if you want. We recommend setting a status like "In onboarding" for first week so people know not to expect quick reviews.

HR-Bot: Reminder: complete your I-9 and benefits forms. Run `/hr status` to see outstanding items.

Aisha: One last practical: should I use threads for follow-ups during meetings?

Claire (eng): During meetings, drop notes in the meeting channel and thread action items. If it's a quick follow-up, a DM is fine. For anything that might help others later, put it in a thread in the channel.

Sam (onboarding): TL;DR for new hires: 1) post intros in #general and longer notes in #new-hires, 2) file access tickets in #help and tag @it, 3) CI/build/large logs -> #eng-builds with links, 4) use reactions to reduce noise, 5) set timezone & status. Ping me or @people-ops if anything is unclear.

Aisha: Thanks everyone 1 appreciate the clarity. Opening a gist for my test logs and will post in #eng-builds.
